claimedRepairs.verification: v1 pinned '$.decisions.P-1' and '$.decisions.P-2' in dot form. Both keys contain a hyphen, which makes the dot form ambiguous as JSONPath — the segment can parse as a subtraction expression rather than a literal member name — so the selector was not reliably resolvable even though the underlying decisions existed. v2 pins '$.decisions["P-1"]' and '$.decisions["P-2"]'. G3-SUBSTRATE was already in bracket form. I confirmed all three selectors are well-formed and that each resolves to a real key in the product packet's decisions object.

claimedRepairs.verification: v2's enforcementHonesty now routes qualification to 'DR-G07, DR-G08 (scoped to root/index/core/component install trust; repair-media/self-update rollback defer with DR-110), DR-G09, DR-G21, and DR-128 as applicable.' File 08 records DR-G08 TRUST-RECOVERY as 'Root/index/core/component/repair trust survives expiry, revocation, quorum loss, rollback' across 'online/offline/air-gap/removable-media' states, and DR-110 as 'Core self-update/repair/rollback and repair-media trust'. The two rows genuinely overlap on repair, rollback and repair-media, and the candidate's split — invoke DR-G08 for the install-trust surface, defer the repair-media and self-update-rollback surface with DR-110 — is a correct partition of that overlap. It is also consistent with D-002, which lists DR-110 among its named deferrals ('self-update/repair — install is fresh signed download in slice 1').

selfCorrection: The DR-G08 advisory was a real gap in v1 that I did not catch. My v1 verdict checked that the four routed gates — DR-G07, DR-G09, DR-G21, DR-128 — existed in the corpus, and reported that they did. What I never asked was whether the routing list was complete, and DR-G08 TRUST-RECOVERY covers root/index/core/component trust, which is precisely the trust surface a non-admission posture leans on. This is the same failure mode I have hit before in this engagement: verifying that each cited thing resolves without verifying that the set of citations is the right set. Existence checks confirm nothing about completeness, and a qualification-routing list is exactly the kind of clause where the omission, not the entry, is the defect. I am recording it here because v2 is where the correction lands.

acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. Both repairs landed and both were worth making — neither is cosmetic. The selector change fixes JSONPath that was ambiguous precisely because these decision ids contain hyphens, and the DR-G08 addition closes a completeness gap in the qualification routing that I missed at v1 by checking that the cited gates existed rather than asking whether the citation set was right. I have recorded that as a self-correction. Everything I verified from source at v1 compares byte-identical here, and I re-tested selector-set completeness against file 08's own pins rather than assuming the edit left it sound: DR-010 pins exactly the three decisions the candidate selects, with CD-RT-5 belonging to the DR-001 and DR-008 pins and correctly left untouched.
